title: CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid

paragraphs.en: Diana suggested, "Of course you must be Elaine, Anne. I couldn't have the courage to float down there alone."
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜提议说：“当然你得扮演埃琳，安妮。我可没勇气独自下去。”

paragraphs.en: Ruby shivered, agreeing, "Nor could I. It's fun when we're together, but lying down pretending to be dead—no way."
paragraphs.zh: ruby打了个寒战，附和道：“我也做不到。在一起的时候挺有趣的，但假装躺下装死——不可能。”

paragraphs.en: Jane added, "It would be romantic, but I'd keep peeking up every minute to check my position and not drift too far."
paragraphs.zh: 简补充道：“这样听起来挺浪漫，但我每分钟都会偷偷向上看，检查自己的位置，以免漂得太远。”

paragraphs.en: Anne lamented, "A red-haired Elaine is ridiculous. But Ruby should be Elaine; she has fair skin and long golden hair like the lily maid."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹息道：“红头发的埃琳娜真是荒谬。但Ruby应该叫埃琳娜，她皮肤白皙，金发长如百合少女。”

paragraphs.en: Diana pointed out, "Your complexion is as fair as Ruby's, and your hair is darker now after you cut it."
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜指出：“你的肤色跟鲁比的一样白皙，剪了头发之后，头发反而更黑了。”

paragraphs.en: Anne was delighted, "Do you really think so? I've always thought it might be me—but never dared to ask. Could my hair be called auburn now, Diana?"
paragraphs.zh: 安妮高兴地说：“你真的这么认为吗？我一直觉得可能是我——但从来不敢问。戴安娜，我的头发现在可以叫红褐色了吗？”

paragraphs.en: Diana admired Anne’s short, silky curls, saying, "Yes, and it looks pretty with the jaunty black velvet ribbon."
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜羡慕安妮那短而柔滑的卷发，说道：“是啊，配上那根时髦的黑色丝带显得格外精神。”

paragraphs.en: They stood by the pond below Orchard Slope, where birches lined a small headland jutting into the water. Ruby and Jane were visiting Diana, while Anne came to play.
paragraphs.zh: 她们站在果园坡下面的小池塘边，那里有一片白桦树沿着一个小突出的岬角伸向水面。鲁比和简来看望戴安娜，而安妮则是来玩耍的。

paragraphs.en: Anne and Diana had spent much of their summer playing by the pond. Mr. Bell cut down the trees in his pasture, leaving Anne to weep among the stumps but quickly finding new activities like fishing for trout and rowing a dory.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮和戴安娜的夏天大多时候都在池塘边玩耍。贝尔回先生砍伐了牧场里的树木，这让安妮在树桩间流下了眼泪，但很快她便找到了新的乐趣，比如钓鲑鱼和划独木舟。

paragraphs.en: Inspired by Tennyson's "Lily Maid of Astolat," Anne suggested they dramatize Elaine’s story. They had dissected the poem in school, making it seem less meaningful, yet Elaine, Lancelot, Guinevere, and King Arthur became vivid characters to them. Anne wished she could have been born in Camelot.
paragraphs.zh: 受泰尼森《阿斯托拉特的百合女仆》的启发，安妮建议她们将埃琳的故事搬上舞台。在学校里，他们曾对这首诗进行了详细的分析，使其显得意义不大，但埃琳、兰斯洛特、桂妮薇儿和亚瑟王在她们心中却栩栩如生。安妮希望自己能出生在卡米洛特。

paragraphs.en: Anne would be Elaine, though reluctantly, as her artistic sense required a more fitting role. Diana was King Arthur, Jane played Guinevere, and Diana also took on the roles of Lancelot, brothers, and their father. They needed only black material for the barge; Diana’s mother's old shawl sufficed.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮虽然不情愿，但为了符合她的艺术感，她将扮演埃琳。戴安娜则成了亚瑟王，简饰演桂妮薇尔，而戴安娜还分饰了兰斯洛特、兄弟们以及他们的父亲等角色。他们只需要黑色的布料来制作小船；戴安娜的母亲旧披肩正好派上用场。

paragraphs.en: Anne spread the shawl over the flat-bottomed dory and lay down inside it, eyes closed and hands folded across her chest.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮把围巾铺在平底的划艇上，然后躺了进去，双眼紧闭，双手叠放在胸前。

paragraphs.en: Ruby Gillis whispered nervously, "She does look really dead." Anne replied sternly, "Ruby, you shouldn't talk about Mrs. Lynde. This is long before she was born."
paragraphs.zh: ruby 吉里斯紧张地小声说道：“她确实看起来死了。”安妮严厉地说：“ruby，你不应该提起雷切尔·林德太太。这可是她出生很久之前的事了。”

paragraphs.en: Jane stepped in, arranging a yellow Japanese crepe scarf as a coverlet and placing a blue iris in Anne's hand to mimic a white lily.
paragraphs.zh: 简走了进来，她把一条黄色的日本绉绸围巾当作被单铺好，并递给安妮一朵蓝色的鸢尾花，模仿白色的百合。

paragraphs.en: "Now, she’s ready," Jane said. "Kiss her quiet brows, Diana, and say 'Sister, farewell forever.' Ruby, say 'Farewell, sweet sister,' both with sorrow."
paragraphs.zh: “现在她准备好了，”简说道，“戴安娜，亲吻她的宁静额头，说声‘姐姐，永别了’。鲁比，你也说声‘再见，亲爱的姐姐’，带着悲伤。”

paragraphs.en: Anne smiled slightly, remembering Elaine's smile-like pose. The flat was pushed off, scraping over an old stake.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮微微一笑，想起埃琳那像微笑般姿态的情景。木板被推开了，刮过一根旧木桩。

paragraphs.en: Diana, Jane, and Ruby quickly scampered through the woods to the lower headland where they awaited Lancelot, Guinevere, and the King.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜、简和鲁比迅速穿过树林，来到了较低的岬角上，她们在那里等候兰塞洛特、桂妮薇儿和国王。

paragraphs.en: For a moment, Anne enjoyed the romance of her situation. Then reality hit—water began leaking into the flat. She scrambled up, grabbed the coverlet and pall, and saw a big crack at the bottom.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮一时沉浸在这一幕的浪漫中，但很快现实便迎面而来——水开始渗进屋内。她急忙爬起，抓过床单和被罩，发现底部裂开了一道大缝。

paragraphs.en: Anne gasped but remained calm. There was one chance: she could row back to the landing for oars.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮倒抽了一口气，但还是保持镇定。她心中闪过一丝希望：可以划船返回岸边取桨。

paragraphs.en: She told Mrs. Allan she was terrified that day. As the flat drifted toward the bridge, water rose rapidly inside it. She prayed fervently, repeating, "Dear God, please bring the flat close to a pile."
paragraphs.zh: 她告诉艾伦太太那天自己非常害怕。随着小船向桥靠近，里面迅速灌满了水。她虔诚地祈祷着：“亲爱的上帝，请让小船靠近一个系缆柱。”

paragraphs.en: The flat bumped against a pile, and she quickly climbed up an old tree trunk. Clinging tightly, she knew she needed human help to reach safety.
paragraphs.zh: 扁平的物体撞上了一堆东西，她迅速爬上了老树干。紧紧抓住树干，她知道自己需要人类的帮助才能安全脱险。

paragraphs.en: The girls on the lower headland saw the flat sink midstream. Ruby, Jane, and Diana ran through the woods in panic, not stopping until they reached the bridge. Anne heard their screams and saw them dash by.
paragraphs.zh: 绿山墙那片低地上的女孩们看见木筏在河中央沉了下去。鲁比、简和戴安娜慌忙穿过树林，直到跑到桥边才停了下来。安妮听见她们的尖叫，看到她们飞奔而过。

paragraphs.en: Help was coming soon, but her position was precarious.
paragraphs.zh: 援助很快就会到来，但她目前的处境却相当危险。

paragraphs.en: Anne sat by the riverbank, her arms aching, as minutes felt like hours. Suddenly, Gilbert Blythe appeared in Harmon Andrews’s dory.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮坐在河岸边，双臂酸痛难忍，感觉时间仿佛凝固。就在这时，吉尔伯特·布雷思突然出现在哈蒙·安德鲁斯的独木舟里。

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley! How did you get there?" he exclaimed, surprised to see her.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·谢里登！你怎么会在这里？”他惊讶地脱口而出。

paragraphs.en: Without waiting for an answer, he pulled close and offered his hand. Anne clung to it, scrambling down into the boat. She sat, dripping and furious, holding a wet shawl and crepe in her arms.
paragraphs.zh: 他顾不上等回答，一把拉近自己，伸出手来。安妮紧紧握住他的手，急忙爬进小船里。她坐在里面，浑身湿透且气愤不已，怀里抱着一块湿漉漉的围巾和一束水淋淋的百合花。

paragraphs.en: "What happened?" Gilbert asked as they rowed towards the landing.
paragraphs.zh: “发生了什么事？”吉尔伯特一边划船靠岸一边问道。

paragraphs.en: Anne explained frigidly that she had been playing Elaine and drifted to Camelot in a barge, which leaked. The girls went for help while she climbed onto the pile. Gilbert rowed them to the landing, and Anne, disdainful of his assistance, leaped ashore.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮冷冷地解释说，她扮演的是埃琳，并乘着一条漏水的小船飘到了卡米洛特。女孩们去求助时，她自己爬上了堆物。吉尔伯特划船把她们送到岸边，安妮不屑于他的帮助，跳下了船。

paragraphs.en: "Thank you," she said haughtily before turning away. But Gilbert followed her, placing a hand on her arm.
paragraphs.zh: “谢谢，”她傲慢地说着，随即转身离去。但吉尔伯特紧跟其后，在她的手臂上轻轻按了一下。

paragraphs.en: "Anne," he hurriedly said, "can we be friends? I’m sorry for making fun of your hair. It was just a joke and it’s been so long.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，”他急忙说道，“我们可以做朋友吗？我为开你的头发玩笑向你道歉。那只是个笑话，都已经过去很久了。”

paragraphs.en: Your hair looks pretty now—honestly."
paragraphs.zh: 你的头发现在看起来挺不错的——说实话。

paragraphs.en: Anne hesitated briefly but then felt a strange mix of emotions. Gilbert Blythe’s half-shy, half-eager look in his hazel eyes was something she found oddly pleasing. However, her old resentment quickly resurfaced.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮犹豫了一下，但随即感到一种复杂的情绪交织在一起。吉尔伯特·布雷思的棕色眼睛里流露出半是羞涩、半是渴望的眼神，让她觉得有些异样地舒心。然而，她旧日的怨恨很快又涌上心头。

paragraphs.en: She remembered the scene from two years ago vividly—Gilbert had called her "carrots" and humiliated her before everyone at school. Her hatred for him remained unchanged by time.
paragraphs.zh: 她清晰地记得两年前的一幕——吉尔伯特当着全校师生的面叫她“胡萝卜”，羞辱了她一番。对他的仇恨随着时间的流逝并未消减。

paragraphs.en: "No," Anne said coldly, "I shall never be friends with you, Gilbert Blythe; and I don't want to be!"
paragraphs.zh: “不，”安妮冷冰冰地说，“我永远也不会和你吉尔伯特·布雷思韦特成为朋友了；而且我也巴不得呢！”

paragraphs.en: "All right!" Gilbert replied angrily, his cheeks flushed. "I'll never ask you to be friends again, Anne Shirley.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧！”吉尔伯特气愤地回答，脸颊涨得通红。“我再也不要求你做我的朋友了，安妮·谢里夫。

paragraphs.en: And I don't care either!"
paragraphs.zh: “我才不在意呢！”

paragraphs.en: He rowed away swiftly, while Anne climbed the steep path under the maples. She held her head high but felt a strange regret. She almost wished she had responded differently.
paragraphs.zh: 他划着船迅速离开了，安妮则沿着枫树下的陡峭小径攀登而上。她昂首挺胸，但内心却感到一种奇怪的后悔。她几乎希望自己当时能做出不同的回应。

paragraphs.en: Despite the insult, there was still something that tugged at her.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管受到了侮辱，但她心里还是有些触动。

paragraphs.en: Halfway up, Jane and Diana rushed back from their search, nearly hysterical. They hadn't found anyone at Orchard Slope; both Mr. and Mrs. Barry were away. Ruby Gillis had broken down in hysterics, left to recover alone.
paragraphs.zh: 半途而废，简和戴安娜从搜寻中狂乱地跑了回来。她们在果园坡并没有找到任何人；巴里先生和太太都外出不在家。鲁比·吉尔思哭得一塌糊涂，被独自留下，只能自己慢慢恢复。

paragraphs.en: Jane and Diana had raced through the Haunted Wood and across the brook to Green Gables, where they also found no one—Marilla was in Carmody, and Matthew was making hay.
paragraphs.zh: 简和戴安娜疾驰穿过幽暗森林，跨过小溪，赶到绿山墙农舍。但这里也没有人——玛丽拉去了卡姆多伊，而马修正在割草。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Anne," gasped Diana, falling into her arms and weeping with relief, "oh, Anne—we thought—you were—drowned—and we felt like murderers—because we had made—you be—Elaine. And Ruby is in hysterics—oh, Anne, how did you escape?"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，”戴安娜喘着气，扑进她的怀里，带着如释重负的泪水说道，“安妮，我们以为——你被淹死了——我们都觉得自己是杀人犯——因为我们让你变成了埃琳。而鲁比现在正在歇斯底里地哭喊——哦，安妮，你是怎么逃出来的？”

paragraphs.en: "I climbed up on one of the piles," explained Anne wearily, "and Gilbert Blythe came along in Mr. Andrews's dory and brought me to land."
paragraphs.zh: “我爬到了一根木桩上，”安妮疲惫地解释说，“吉尔伯特·布莱斯驾着安德鲁斯先生的划艇跟了过来，并把我送上了岸。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Anne, how splendid of him! Why, it's so romantic!" said Jane, finally finding her voice.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，他真是太浪漫了！天哪，这简直太富有诗意了！”简终于开口说道。

paragraphs.en: "Of course you'll speak to him after this."
paragraphs.zh: “当然你之后会和他说话的。”

paragraphs.en: Anne declared she would not and vowed never to hear the word 'romantic' again from Jane Andrews. She apologized for frightening her friends and blamed herself for their troubles. Her intuition proved correct; the Barrys and Cuthberts were shocked by the day's events.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮坚决表示不会再说下去，并发誓再也不听简·安德鲁斯提起“浪漫”这个词。她为吓到朋友们而道歉，责怪自己给他们带来了麻烦。她的直觉果然没错；巴里一家和卡特伯一家对当天发生的事情感到震惊。

paragraphs.en: "Will you ever have any sense, Anne?" Marilla groaned.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你什么时候才能有点理智？”玛丽拉叹了口气。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, I think so," Anne replied optimistically after a good cry in solitude. "I believe my chances of becoming sensible are better now."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我相信如此，”安妮在独处时流完眼泪后乐观地回答，“我觉得我现在变得更理智的机会更大了。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla was skeptical. Anne explained that each mistake at Green Gables had taught her something valuable. The amethyst brooch incident taught her not to meddle; the Haunted Wood episode curbed her imagination; the liniment cake mishap improved her cooking; dyeing her hair reduced her vanity.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉对此表示怀疑。安妮解释说，绿山墙农舍中的每一次失误都教会了她一些宝贵的东西。紫水晶胸针事件让她学会了不要多管闲事；幽灵林事件则抑制了她的想象力；药膏蛋糕的事故提高了她的烹饪技巧；染发的经历则减少了她的虚荣心。

paragraphs.en: Today, she realized romance no longer suited Avonlea.
paragraphs.zh: 今天，她意识到浪漫已不再适合埃文利了。

paragraphs.en: "Don't give up all your romance, Anne," Matthew whispered. "A little is good—not too much—but keep a little of it."
paragraphs.zh: “不要放弃所有的浪漫，安妮，”马修低语道，“留一点好的就够了——不要太夸张，但还是要保留一些。”
